attributes.body:
大体（だいたい） is an adverb that is used to highlight the 'main point' of something in Japanese, and therefore has several different nuances. 大体（だいたい） will regularly be translated as 'mostly', 'generally', or 'for the most part'.

As with other adverbs that highlight amounts, 大体（だいたい） can be used to modify entire phrases, or can be used directly before a noun as 大体（だいたい）の + noun.

In a similar way to そもそも, a noun/adverb which means 'in the first place', 大体（だいたい） can also have this meaning. This nuance is frequently quite obvious, as the rest of the sentence will highlight a desired outcome that unfortunately did not happen.

Although these 2 primary uses of 大体（だいたい） may seem quite different, they are both just expressing what is 'essentially' correct, most common, the original, etc.

Fun Fact

A common synonym for 大体（だいたい） is 根本（ねもと）, a noun which means 'the source', or 'the origin' of something. In this way, 大体（だいたい） just expresses the way something is, without receiving any alterations (regardless of whether any subsequent alterations are positive or negative). This is where the 'in essence' meaning comes from.

These can be used interchangeably to express roughly or about. だいたい is more casual and common in daily speech, as in だいたい百人来た (About a hundred people came). おおよそ sounds slightly more formal or written, as in おおよそ見当がつく (I can roughly guess). Note that だいたい can also appear as a negative interjection, as in だいたい何でいるの？ (Why are you here in the first place?), while おおよそ cannot be used this way.3

attributes.body: Both だいたい and ほとんど can express 'most' or 'almost all,' but they also have distinct uses. For example, だいたいの人 and ほとんどの人 both mean 'most people', and だいたい一緒 and ほとんど一緒 both mean 'almost the same'. However, they diverge when ほとんど is used negatively as in ほとんどない 'almost none', as well as when だいたい means 'generally' or 'approximately' (だいたい５時に起きる), as ほとんど cannot be used here.

attributes.body: Both can mean 'most', as in だいたいの人／おおよその人 'most people'. They can also both mean 'approximately', e.g. だいたい３時間／おおよそ３時間 'about three hours'. However, おおよそ is much more formal and mainly used in writing. だいたい can also express 'in the first place', e.g. だいたいなんでいるの？ ('Why are you here in the first place?)' or 'roughly/adequately', e.g. だいたいでいいから ('Roughly is fine.), while おおよそ cannot.
